# An `open_prepayment:` summary somebody edited by hand, in four ways.
#
# The block is informational and derived — the importer rebuilds credits from
# the per-split `lot_owner:` KVPs and never from this summary — so a
# disagreement is a warning and the next export rewrites the figure. That is
# only true if every shape a person can leave behind is read as a shape rather
# than as a figure: a block naming no owner, an amount that is not a number,
# and a block on an account this book does not have are all things a half
# finished edit leaves, and reading any of them as a number would have the
# import warn about a credit nobody declared.
#
# What this fixture produces: one customer credit of 50.00 on the receivable,
# and a summary declaring
#   - 30.00 for C-EDIT, which is wrong and must be warned about;
#   - a block naming neither customer nor vendor;
#   - a block whose amount is a word.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_a_hand_edited_prepayment_summary_is_not_read_as_figures.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	open_prepayment:
		customer: "C-EDIT"
		amount: 30.00 CAD
	open_prepayment:
		amount: 10.00 CAD
	open_prepayment:
		customer: "C-EDIT"
		amount: about fifty

customer "C-EDIT"
	name: "Hand Edit Customer"
	currency: CAD

2026-01-05 * "Deposit on account"
	Assets:Bank 50.00 CAD
	Assets:Accounts Receivable -50.00 CAD
		lot_owner: "customer:C-EDIT"
